decisions.evidence: Entries 5-6: maker presents saving via “link address” and Save; client says the “basic save-and-appear flow matches.”

decisions.evidence: Entries 5-6: the initial form has manually entered title and no collected description; client asks for automatically filled title/description “while still being able to edit them.”

decisions.evidence: Entries 7-8: maker presents “paste → fields appear → edit → save”; client says editing before saving “is important.”

decisions.evidence: Entries 9-10: maker says search covers title and description and “does not currently match” the address; client requests address search and adds that personal notes must also be searched.

decisions.evidence: Entries 13-14: maker offers Version 1 with exactly one topic versus Version 2 with several; client selects Version 2 because a link can belong to several topics.

decisions.evidence: Entries 13-14: maker presents clicking a topic button or topic on a link to filter; client says clicking any topic to filter “feels right.”

decisions.evidence: Entries 7-8 and 13-14: entries show title, description, and favicon, and the later topic version shows topic tags; the client approves both revisions.

decisions.evidence: Entries 19-20: when fetching fails, maker still saves the URL and permits a manual title; client explicitly prefers that fallback.

decisions.evidence: Entries 21-22: maker presents Edit loading a link’s details into the existing form for changes and Update; client accepts the management flow.

decisions.evidence: Entries 21-22: maker presents permanent deletion after confirmation; client says Delete should permanently remove the link after confirmation.
